entities.summary:
CRC Press, founded in 1903 in Boca Raton, Florida, has emerged as a pivotal institution in the realm of scholarly publishing, particularly in the fields of science, technology, and medicine. The company was established by Samuel C. CRC Press, and has played a crucial role in disseminating vital research and educational materials across North America and beyond. Its significance lies in its commitment to high-quality, peer-reviewed content, which has supported the advancement of knowledge in various disciplines for over a century.

From its inception, CRC Press has published thousands of books and journals, becoming a key player in the academic and professional publishing landscape. It introduced innovative series such as the "Chemical and Physical Data" series and the "Handbook of Chemistry and Physics," which provided essential data for scientists. The company also embraced emerging technologies, transitioning to digital formats and expanding its reach through online resources, which facilitated access to crucial information for researchers and practitioners.

The legacy of CRC Press extends beyond mere publication; it has influenced the way research is communicated and how knowledge is shared globally. As a subsidiary of the Taylor & Francis Group since 2000, it continues to shape scholarly discourse, impacting countless researchers, educators, and professionals worldwide. The institution's commitment to high standards in publishing has left an indelible mark on academia, fostering an environment where knowledge can thrive and evolve.

Today, CRC Press stands as a testament to the power of scholarly publishing, with a catalog that includes over 30,000 titles. As noted by one prominent editor, 'The work we publish not only informs but also inspires innovations across various fields,' highlighting the enduring impact of their contributions to the advancement of science and technology.
